shows.title: American Revolution – Episode 2
shows.excerpt: When Ken Burns presents a history (The Civil War, Jazz, The Roosevelts etc) you know he has done his research. Here, building the narrative from the testimonies of soldiers, townspeople and statesmen, he reveals in impeccable detail how the United States of America was born. Using paintings and maps alongside re-enactments and the input of scholars from many perspectives, he invites us to listen to the participants, imagine the smells, feel the emotions of the enslaved and reflect on the strategies of native peoples. This is a visceral portrait far removed from dry text, giving context to current semiquincentennial celebrations. We are thrilled to welcome Ken Burns to present this episode on the big screen. – Maggi Hurt.

shows.title: Bad Day at the Office
shows.excerpt: Waking up in a strange hotel room with a dead body in the bathtub, police knocking at the door and no memory of the night before, Karl (John Hannah) is about to have a very bad day indeed. Enlisting the help of a sparky hotel maid (Radha Mitchell) he is forced to fight for his life whilst trying to piece together answers as they battle foe after foe across London. Shot in the style of first person shooter video games with cine-literate wit, humour, ferocious pacing and a cracking soundtrack, this is an anarchic, ultra-violent and hilarious thrill ride of pure, cinematic carnage. The ultimate Midnight Madness experience. – Emma Boa

shows.title: Borges and Me
shows.excerpt: In the early 1970s writer and student Jay Parini (Whitehead) finds himself committed to driving blind poet Jorge Luis Borges (Gnecco) across the Scottish countryside. Over the course of an eventful journey the pair form a complex and rich bond, one imbued with poetry, music and melancholy. Beautifully adapted from Parini’s memoir, this gorgeously shot and superbly acted film from director Marc Turtletaub evokes memory, time and place with a remarkably vivid and clear-eyed candour. Featuring terrific supporting performances from Scottish acting legends Alan Cumming, Peter Mullan and Freya Mavor, this is literate and grown-up filmmaking of the highest order. – Paul Ridd

shows.title: Capsized
shows.excerpt: An apparently idyllic house boat trip is thrown into disarray when Diane (Rabe) and her children are rocked by revelations of financial strife kept secret by obstinate husband Ray (Ifans). At sea and with a chaotic holiday ahead of them, the family must struggle to keep it together and face an uncertain future, but not before competing in a truly epic fishing competition. With an easygoing charm, affection for its complex characters, and a real sense of place, Lindsey Ryan’s beautifully filmed and hilarious American indie debut tackles a very contemporary story of economic uncertainty with optimism, warmth and humour. – Paul Ridd

shows.title: Coming Home
shows.excerpt: A US Marine Corps captain’s wife (Jane Fonda) finds herself drawn to a paraplegic war vet (Jon Voight) after her husband (Bruce Dern) leaves to fight in Vietnam. By the time her husband returns from the front, each one of them has changed immeasurably. Conceived and produced by Fonda, Coming Home is one of the earliest films to explore the emotional as well as physical consequences of the Vietnam War. Hal Ashby’s compassionate, insightful indictment of the impacts of the conflict is an authentic, richly observed and deeply moving exploration of disillusionment, guilt and complex trauma, featuring extraordinary performances from its Oscar-winning cast. We are delighted to welcome Bruce Dern to introduce this special screening. – Emma Boa

shows.title: Douglas Gordon by Douglas Gordon
shows.excerpt: Blurring the boundary between documentary and artistic experiment, this hypnotic film immerses audiences in the world of influential Scottish artist Douglas Gordon. Combining archival footage, disorientating imagery and candid exchanges filled with humour and honesty, the film explores artistic identity and the tension between performance and reality. Moments of illness, anger and emotional vulnerability cut through the film’s heightened visual language, revealing a portrait that is both chaotic and deeply human. With striking sound design and hypnotic pacing, this is an experiential and unpredictable reflection on creativity and selfhood. – Ella Novie

shows.title: First Zone
shows.excerpt: Living out existence in an abandoned wind turbine high above an endless ocean, ultra tough Fenna (Minis) has become used to surviving alone in the aftermath of a climate catastrophe. But when a violent storm separates her from home, she embarks on an odyssey across the vast wetlands of a post-apocalyptic landscape. Along the way Fenna will encounter other survivors and begin remembering connection, community and a life before the end of the world. Resourcefully and beautifully shot in real Holland locations, debut director Thom Lunshof’s film is thoughtful and unsettling. A unique, compelling and urgent film for our times. – Paul Ridd

shows.excerpt: When a bullied young schoolboy goes into hiding from his classmates, a lonely girl from his class discovers him and a delicate, respectful relationship begins to form, opening their worlds up in myriad ways. Beautifully shot with painterly compositions, a tactile, textured aesthetic and powered by introspective narration and outstanding performances from its two young leads, Felix de Givry’s debut feature is dreamy, soulful and stirring cinema rooted in adolescent pain and confusion. A subtle, sensitive and beautifully realised story of compassion and acceptance fresh from its World Premiere in Cannes Critics Week. – Emma Boa

shows.title: Hamlet
shows.excerpt: The King of Denmark is dead, and the Queen has married his brother. Prince Hamlet, seeing spirits and feigning madness, seeks out revenge. Famously faithful to the unabridged original text, director and actor Kenneth Branagh’s adaptation boasts a star studded cast and opulent, theatrical visuals. Exploring timeless themes of corruption, truth and madness, Hamlet proves itself as timely as ever in our modern era. A magnificent epic at just over four hours, the film has long been lauded as one of the best adaptations of Shakespeare’s greatest play. – Jack Lennon

shows.title: Her Private Hell
shows.excerpt: Glamorous young actresses are targeted by the killer Leather Man and a vengeful GI searches for his daughter in this hypnotic, ultraviolent film from Nicolas Winding Refn. Set against the backdrop of a surreal, neon soaked city, a bizarre high rise hotel, the violent streets of retrofuturist urban sprawl and extravagant film production sets, this strange, unsettling and deeply beautiful neo-Giallo is an exercise in gleeful filmmaking style. A terrific, pounding new score from regular Brian DePalma collaborator Pino Donaggio is the icing on the cake for fans of psychedelic cinema and baroque excess. Quite simply this is pure cinema. – Paul Ridd

Exploring generational differences, sexual politics and queerness with his customary visual panache, fearlessness and affection, iconic director Araki makes a welcome return to feature filmmaking with this hilarious and weirdly moving battle of the sexes. – Paul Ridd

shows.title: Imposters
shows.excerpt: How far would you go to save your child? This is the moral quandary an on-the-rocks husband and wife face in Caleb J. Phillips’ mind-blowing film. When their child goes missing, Marie and Paul’s already fractious marriage faces its toughest challenge yet. At their wits’ end, Marie stumbles onto a means of finding their baby. What she brings back, however, might not be their son. Tearing through the fabric of their marriage and reality itself, the rabbit hole’s journey gives them far more than they’ve bargained for. Starring Jessica Rothe (Happy Death Day) and Charlie Barnett (Russian Doll), Imposters brings a whole new meaning to “Till Death Do Us Part.” – Brandon Streussnig

shows.excerpt: In Valerie Faris and Jonathan Dayton’s glorious debut feature, a dysfunctional family embark on a ragtag road trip so that 10 year old Olive can compete in a beauty pageant. A breakout smash at Sundance Film Festival in 2006, this is an era-defining American indie comedy brimming with wit, intelligence, humour and a deep empathy for its richly drawn characters. First class performances from a superb cast including Toni Collette, Steve Carell, Greg Kinnear, Paul Dano and Alan Arkin, a sublime score by Mychael Danna and Devotchka and a special 20th anniversary restoration make this a real treat on the big screen. – Emma Boa

shows.title: Mission
shows.excerpt: Dylan (George MacKay) has reached the end of his tether with his dead-end job and lonely, unfulfilling existence. Over the course of a week he blows his life up, pushing boundaries and seeking meaning in the wake of extreme chaos as he wrestles with trying to feel alive and finding a reason to go on. Paul Wright’s immersive, expressionistic portrait of a young man’s existential angst and directionless fury is vividly composed, frenetically paced and fraught with tension. Filmed in Scotland, crackling with anarchic energy and featuring a compelling performance from MacKay, this is a bold, visionary film that demands to be seen on the big screen. -Emma Boa

shows.title: My NDA
shows.excerpt: A gripping observational documentary exposing secrecy as a psychological weapon wielded by corporate America, as three ordinary people choose to break their non-disclosure agreements. This nail-biting film reveals how pervasive public censorship is manipulating justice in every corner of American society. As the legal, public and emotional stakes rise, an intimate lens on each character asks what happens when the most important truths, and those carrying the weight of them, are silenced? -Therese Walsh

shows.excerpt: Frustrated with living out his final days in a nursing home, elderly rogue Arthur (Dern) recruits his uptight grandson Kevin (Parrish) to break him out. Together the pair head north to Canada, picking up an enigmatic stranger (Fox) along the way. Acidly funny, unpredictable and ultimately very moving, this sharply directed and superbly acted film from director William Scoular is a showcase for Bruce Dern’s magnetic screen presence and feeling for a character who positively bursts off the screen. Featuring a final performance from legendary actor Graham Greene as well as superb supporting turns from Joanna Cassidy and Dylan Baker. -Paul Ridd

shows.title: Out There
shows.excerpt: Still grieving the disappearance of her scientist father, amateur teenaged astronomer Maz (Stocks) is convinced she has spotted something suspicious hovering above her sleepy Welsh hometown. Recruiting the support of her best mate Little Elis (Moya), UFO-obsessed conspiracy theorist Bryn (Barnard) and local psychic Shifty Gruff (Sheen), Maz and her gang of misfits set out to uncover the truth, one that is far more complex than they might have expected. Breathlessly paced, wittily evoking its 1999 setting via superb music choices, costumes and production design, this charming Welsh debut from director Simon Ryninks is poignant, funny and entirely unpredictable. -Paul Ridd

shows.title: A Personal Journey with Martin Scorsese Through American Movies
shows.excerpt: Beginning as an exhaustive journey through the origins of Hollywood, moving through the invention and evolution of genres and heralding the work of unsung heroes of classical and modern cinema, Scorsese’s mammoth documentary made with the BFI in 1995 is one of the most richly detailed, fascinating of all cinema essays. Part personal history, part rediscovery, and always imbued with a delight and respect for cinema, this is simply one of the best films about films ever made. We are delighted to present the film in its entirety and to be joined by producer Bob Last for a special introduction. – Paul Ridd

shows.title: Pretty Babies
shows.excerpt: Two young girls flee their hometown drawn by the seductive promise of the Hollywood they imagine from the old classics they idolise. Embarking on a road trip for which they are ill-equipped, the American dream soon fractures as they encounter the dark underbelly of the sex industry and the fabric of their friendship starts to unravel. Tyler Marie-Evans’ stylish, melancholic and jaggedly beautiful debut feature is a compelling, female-centred portrait of vulnerability and disillusionment in a world of artifice. Featuring standout performances, a haunting soundtrack and a bold visual style, this film signals an exciting new voice in cinema.- Emma Boa

shows.title: Queen at Sea
shows.excerpt: When Amanda (Binoche) walks in on her elderly parents in the throes of what appears to be a consensual sexual encounter her instinct is to call the police, believing her mother Leslie (Calder-Marshall) who is suffering from dementia, is incapable of giving consent to husband Martin (Courtenay). As this complex, emotionally devastating and utterly gripping scenario plays out we are asked to question our preconceptions, our ideas and our treatment of the elderly in this devastating and superbly acted film, winner of a Silver Bear at the Berlinale. This is a moral maze filmmaking at its most nuanced and sophisticated. -Paul Ridd

shows.title: Sacred Creatures
shows.excerpt: Three estranged siblings reunite in rural Italy after the middle sister has been released from psychiatric treatment following a breakdown, one she experienced as a deep spiritual awakening. As this troubled young woman behaves more erratically and relationships fracture, the local community takes on an unexpected significance as power dynamics shift and change. Frieda Luk’s artfully composed and highly compelling debut feature is a deftly woven, unpredictable and black-humoured thriller of superstition, idolatry and communal faith with a distinctive magical realist edge. – Emma Boa

shows.title: Sexy Beast
shows.excerpt: Celebrating 25 years since its UK theatrical release, EIFF presents a brand new restoration of this searing directorial debut from Jonathan Glazer (Birth, Under the Skin, The Zone of Interest). When retired gangster Gal (Winstone) is unwillingly approached by his sociopathic former boss (Kingsley) to undertake one last job, a tense, psychological game of cat and mouse plays out. A compact, gritty British gangster thriller featuring electrifying performances from Winstone and Kingsley, who won an Oscar for his explosive, nerve-shredding turn as Teddy Bass, and set against the incongruously sunny backdrop of the Costa del Sol, this is a cinematic treat on the big screen. – Emma Boa

shows.title: Sheep in the Box
shows.excerpt: In an attempt to come to terms with their grief, a couple welcome a humanoid robot version of their deceased son into their home. Under the characteristically subtle and nuanced direction of Kore-Eda, what begins as a thoughtful study of parental emotion and loss subtly transforms into a thematically rich and thorny exploration of artificial intelligence, our responsibility with it and towards it and what the future might look like with this technology as a part of daily life. Part human drama, part grounded sci-fi, this beautifully acted and moving film asks many complex questions whilst never losing its core humanity and pathos. -Paul Ridd

shows.title: Skintown
shows.excerpt: Set in Northern Ireland in 1994 during the IRA ceasefire, best friends Vinny and Jonty party with friends, cut deals and make plans to escape small town life. The uncertainty and instability of the time conspire against them in Kieron J. Walsh’s vivid portrait of disenfranchised youth, 90s rave culture and a turbulent period in recent Irish history. Balancing humour, wit and pathos and bolstered by great performances from a terrific cast including Jack Rowan, Chris Walley, Jamie Lee O’Donnell and Hope Ikpoku Jnr. and a killer 90s soundtrack featuring Prodigy, Elastica, Happy Mondays, Jeff Mills and Carl Cox, this is a propulsive, poignant period piece .- Emma Boa

shows.title: Snapshot
shows.excerpt: Newly unearthed footage from late 19th century London reveals the complex fate of an all-ladies ghost-hunting society in this transfixing horror feature debut from director Joseph Archer. Exploring a dangerous city of contradictions with a new technology potentially capable of capturing malevolent supernatural forces, the film throws us into a world of cruelty, violence and press sensationalism, threat always hovering just around the next corner and at the peripheries of the pinhole camera lens. An inventive reimagining of the found footage genre this uniquely strange, scary and distinctive film is guaranteed to provoke, disturb and thrill in equal measure. -Paul Ridd

shows.title: The Arrow at Rest at Every Instant of its Flight
shows.excerpt: Three seemingly disconnected stories unfold across New York City. Gus Birney stars as Violet, a jaded arcade worker, Sinopia, an upper-class professor bored with her marriage, and Jade, an endlessly cool young woman who decides to help a stranger out of her debt. Meanwhile, a woman with a suitcase (Constance Shulman) moves through the city in search of the doppelganger trying to take over her life. Surreal, comedic and reflexive, this film plays out like free jazz, with writer-director Schaefer deftly pulling us through this whirlwind black-and-white flight of fancy. -Pranamika Subhalaxmi

shows.title: The Best Summer
shows.excerpt: A transfixing documentary from Tamra Davis (Crossroads, CB4, Billy Madison) which offers an unfiltered immersion into archival footage of the electric 1995 Summersault festival, featuring iconic performances and candid interviews with alternative rock legends including The Foo Fighters, Beastie Boys, Pavement, Bikini Kill, Sonic Youth, Kim Deal and more. Offering a unique perspective behind the scenes we catch a glimpse of some of the world’s favourite bands at the height of their careers. Both the legendary and the mundane are explored through candid conversations with groups and artists. An opportunity to relive and plunge into an iconic era of alternative rock which spoke to the universal transcendence of music. – Arouny Prasimay

shows.title: The Education of Jane Cumming
shows.excerpt: In early nineteenth-century Edinburgh, two women run a girls’ boarding school, trying to build an independent life in a world with little room for women outside convention. When a wealthy grandmother enrols her granddaughters, including 15-year-old Jane Cumming, the school’s fragile balance begins to shift. Jane’s isolation, the teachers’ concern and the pressures of respectability soon lead to an accusation that changes all their lives. Based on true events, Sophie Heldman’s beautifully made period drama explores prejudice, reputation and the cost of surviving in a strict and unforgiving society. – Annita Nitsaidou

Winner of the NEXT Innovator Award at the Sundance Film Festival, this is a delightful and moving comedy about loneliness, connection and the unknown. – Paul Ridd

shows.title: The Mad World of Harvey Kurtzman
shows.excerpt: A vivid, immersive and visually striking portrait of the founder of the satirical publication Mad magazine and its far-reaching influence on some of the most prominent artists of our time. Kurtzman’s commitment to integrity and challenging the status quo with humour, edge and resilience is a hymn for our times. Rich in historical context, artistic expression, contemporary politics and artfully weaving thoughtful reflections from contributors including Terry Gilliam, the late Stan Lee and Robert Crumb, this is a compelling, insightful exploration of counterculture, commerce and creative compromise and the power of conviction in raw truth and honesty. – Emma Boa

shows.title: Visitor Q
shows.excerpt: An enigmatic stranger falls in with a messed-up family, leaving them forever changed in this shocking explosion of social taboos, casual violence and perverse sexuality. Cult filmmaker Takeshi Miike (AUDITION, ICHI THE KILLER and 13 ASSASSINS) directs this darkly subversive masterpiece of extreme cinema, screening for the first time in decades from a new scan from Radiance Films. – Paul Ridd
